records.name: Ad-Hoc Permission Checks
records.definition: Authorization logic scattered inline throughout the codebase instead of centralized, leaving checks inconsistent and easy to omit.

records.name: Ambient-Credential Trust
records.definition: Treating any request that carries ambient credentials, such as a session cookie, as legitimate without verifying its origin or intent.

records.name: Anonymous Sensitive Access
records.definition: Permitting access to sensitive resources without first establishing the caller's identity.

records.name: Assumption-Driven Security

distinctFrom.reason: Assumption-driven security defends against threats nobody analyzed, while security theater shows controls that do not reduce the real threat.

records.definition: Designing defenses around assumed threats rather than a deliberate analysis of realistic attack vectors.

records.name: Authenticated-Equals-Authorized

distinctFrom.reason: Authenticated-equals-authorized skips the permission check, while authorization scattering spreads the checks with no central policy.

records.definition: Conflating authentication with authorization, so any authenticated caller is granted access without a permission check.

records.name: Broad Admin Access
records.definition: Granting sweeping administrative privileges by default instead of the least access each role requires.

records.name: Hardcoded Rules
records.definition: Embedding access rules directly in code, so changing policy requires a code change and cannot respond to runtime attributes.

records.name: Hardcoded Secrets

distinctFrom.reason: Hardcoded secrets are credentials embedded in source, while secret sprawl is credentials scattered across code, logs and configuration.

records.definition: Embedding credentials, keys, or tokens directly in source or configuration, exposing them to anyone who can read it.

records.name: Immortal Client-Trusted Session
records.definition: A session that never expires and is trusted from client-supplied state alone, so a captured token grants indefinite access.

records.name: Insecure Defaults
records.definition: Shipping default settings that favor convenience over safety, leaving a system exposed unless it is explicitly hardened.

records.name: Manual-Only Review
records.definition: Relying solely on human review to catch policy violations, which neither scales nor reliably covers every case.

records.name: Plaintext Sensitive Storage
records.definition: Storing sensitive data unencrypted at rest, exposing it to anyone who reaches the underlying storage.

records.name: Plaintext Transport
records.definition: Sending data over an unencrypted channel, exposing it to interception and tampering in transit.

records.name: Point-in-Time Audit Only
records.definition: Verifying compliance only at isolated audit moments, leaving the intervals between checks unmonitored for drift.

records.name: Raw Output Rendering
records.definition: Emitting untrusted data into output without encoding it for its context, enabling injection attacks such as cross-site scripting.

records.name: Security as Afterthought
records.definition: Deferring security concerns until late in development, when vulnerabilities are costly and difficult to remediate.

records.name: Single Control Reliance
records.definition: Depending on one security control with no layered defenses, so a single bypass compromises the whole system.

records.name: String-Concatenated SQL
records.definition: Assembling SQL queries by concatenating untrusted input into strings, opening the system to SQL injection.

records.name: Trusted Internal Network Assumption
records.definition: Assuming that traffic originating inside the network perimeter is inherently trustworthy, ignoring insider and lateral-movement threats.

records.name: Trusting External Input
records.definition: Accepting external input as well-formed and safe without validating it, exposing the system to malformed or malicious data.

records.name: Unbounded Autonomy
records.definition: Allowing an actor or component to act without governance limits, so unsafe or unauthorized actions go unchecked.

records.name: Uncontrolled Change
records.definition: Permitting changes to a controlled system without review, approval, or record, undermining compliance and traceability.

records.name: Unnecessary Public Surface
records.definition: Exposing more endpoints, ports, or interfaces publicly than the function requires, enlarging the attack surface.

records.name: Unrestricted Access
records.definition: Permitting access to a resource with no controls, so any caller can invoke any operation.

records.name: Assets

distinctFrom.reason: Assets are the things worth protecting, while threat scenarios are the ways an attacker might reach them.

records.definition: The data, systems, and capabilities of value that a threat model enumerates as the things worth protecting.

records.name: Attribute Definitions
records.definition: Declared descriptions of the subject, resource, action, and environment attributes that an access policy evaluates.

records.name: Authenticated Principal
records.definition: The verified identity of the user or service on whose behalf a request executes, against which permissions are checked.

records.name: Authorization Policy
records.definition: The declared set of rules determining which principals may perform which actions on which resources.

records.name: Consent/Policy
records.definition: The recorded permission and governing rules under which personal data may lawfully be collected and processed.

records.name: Context-Aware Encoding
records.definition: Choosing an output encoding matched to the destination context, such as HTML, an attribute, a URL or a script, so data is neutralized wherever it lands.

records.name: Continuous Authorization
records.definition: The practice of re-verifying a caller's authorization on every request rather than trusting a single earlier check.

records.name: Controls
records.definition: The safeguards and countermeasures put in place to reduce security or compliance risk to an acceptable level.

records.name: Data Minimization
records.definition: Collecting and retaining only the personal data strictly necessary for a stated purpose.

records.name: Defined Policy
records.definition: An explicit, declared set of rules specifying what is permitted or denied, against which enforcement acts.

records.name: Evidence Automation
records.definition: The ability to generate and collect compliance evidence automatically from live systems rather than assembling it by hand.

records.name: Identity Proof
records.definition: The evidence a principal presents to establish its identity, such as a password, token, or certificate.

records.name: Key Management
records.definition: The activity of generating, distributing, rotating, and revoking cryptographic keys across their lifecycle.

records.name: Layered Controls
records.definition: The requirement that multiple independent safeguards protect a resource, so no single failure exposes it.

records.name: Machine-Readable Policies
records.definition: Security or compliance policies expressed in a structured, executable format that tools can evaluate directly.

records.name: Minimal Exposure
records.definition: The condition of exposing only the endpoints, ports, and capabilities strictly required.

records.name: Minimal Permissions
records.definition: The requirement that each principal hold only the permissions its function needs.

records.name: Mitigation
records.definition: The activity of reducing a risk's likelihood or impact through deliberate countermeasures.

records.name: Policy Engine
records.definition: A runtime component that evaluates access requests against declared policies and returns permit or deny decisions.

records.name: Query Parameter Binding
records.definition: Passing query values as bound parameters separate from the query text, so input can never alter the query structure.

records.name: Request Origin Verification
records.definition: Confirming that a state-changing request originates from a trusted client, typically via a token or origin check.

records.name: Review
records.definition: The activity of examining a change or artifact against standards before it is accepted.

records.name: Risk Identification

distinctFrom.reason: Risk identification finds the risks, while mitigation reduces them.

records.definition: The activity of discovering and cataloguing the risks that could affect a system or objective.

records.name: Role Definitions
records.definition: Declared sets of permissions grouped into named roles that are assigned to principals.

records.name: Rotation Policy
records.definition: The specified interval and procedure by which secrets or keys must be replaced to limit the value of any single compromise.

records.name: Secret Store
records.definition: A dedicated, access-controlled repository that holds credentials and keys outside of application code.

records.name: Threat Scenarios
records.definition: Concrete descriptions of how an attacker might attempt to compromise a system, enumerated during threat modeling.

records.name: TLS/mTLS
records.definition: Transport-layer protocols that encrypt a connection and, with mutual TLS, mutually authenticate both endpoints.

records.name: Trust Boundaries
records.definition: The demarcations in a system where the level of trust changes and data crossing them must be validated.

records.name: Strong Identity
records.definition: The requirement that every actor prove a strong, verified identity before any access is granted.

records.name: Validation Rules
records.definition: Declared constraints that input must satisfy, such as type, range, format and length, before it is accepted.

records.name: Automated Control
records.definition: The ability to enforce rules automatically at runtime without manual intervention.

records.name: Bounded Session Lifetime
records.definition: The degree to which a session's validity is time-limited so that access does not persist indefinitely.

records.name: Coarse-Grained Permission Management
records.definition: The ability to manage access by assigning broad, role-level permission sets rather than per-individual grants.

records.name: Compromise Containment
records.definition: The ability to keep a breach confined to one layer or segment so it cannot spread system-wide.

records.name: Confidentiality

distinctFrom.reason: Confidentiality keeps data from being read, while integrity keeps it from being altered.

records.definition: The degree to which data is kept secret from all but authorized parties.

records.name: Confidentiality of Stored Data
records.definition: The degree to which data held at rest remains unreadable to anyone without authorized access.

records.name: Context-Aware Authorization
records.definition: The ability to base access decisions on the runtime context of a request, such as its attributes, its environment and the resource's state.

records.name: Control Selection
records.definition: The activity of choosing which security controls to apply based on identified threats and their priority.

records.name: Data Protection
records.definition: The ability to safeguard data against unauthorized access, loss, or disclosure throughout its lifecycle.

records.name: Fine-Grained Access Control
records.definition: The ability to grant or deny access at a precise level using specific attributes rather than broad roles.

records.name: Forged-Request Rejection
records.definition: The ability to detect and reject requests that a user did not intentionally initiate.

records.name: Identity-Aware Authorization
records.definition: The ability to make access decisions grounded in a verified caller identity.

records.name: Injection Prevention
records.definition: The ability to stop untrusted input from being interpreted as executable code or commands.

records.name: Injection-Safe Data Access
records.definition: The ability to query data such that input can never be interpreted as part of the query structure.

records.name: Integrity
records.definition: The degree to which data is protected from unauthorized or undetected alteration.

records.name: Ongoing Assurance
records.definition: The ability to demonstrate continuously that controls remain effective, rather than only at audit time.

records.name: Perimeterless Security
records.definition: A security model that trusts no network location implicitly and verifies every request regardless of origin.

records.name: Priority-Based Controls
records.definition: The ability to apply controls in order of risk priority, addressing the greatest exposure first.

records.name: Privacy Compliance
records.definition: The degree to which a system meets the privacy obligations imposed by law and policy.

records.name: Proactive Risk Reduction
records.definition: The ability to reduce risk by designing safeguards in from the start rather than patching flaws later.

records.name: Reduced Blast Radius
records.definition: The degree to which the impact of a compromise is confined to a limited scope.

records.name: Reduced Exploitability
records.definition: The degree to which fewer exposed features leave a system harder to exploit.

records.name: Reduced Misconfiguration Risk
records.definition: The degree to which safe defaults lower the chance of an insecure configuration.

records.name: Regulatory Alignment
records.definition: The degree to which a system conforms to the laws and regulations that govern it.

records.name: Resource Protection
records.definition: The ability to ensure that only permitted operations reach a protected resource.

records.name: Revocable Access
records.definition: The ability to withdraw a principal's access immediately when a session or grant is terminated.

records.name: Safe Credential Handling
records.definition: The ability to store, transmit, and use credentials without exposing them.

records.name: Safe Rendering
records.definition: The ability to display untrusted data without allowing it to execute as markup or script.

records.name: Secure Communication
records.definition: The ability to exchange data over a channel protected from interception and tampering.

records.name: Secure Configuration
records.definition: The degree to which a system's settings and secrets are arranged to minimize exposure.

records.name: Zero Trust
records.definition: A security stance that grants no implicit trust and continuously verifies every access request regardless of its source.

records.name: Analytics/Personalization
records.definition: The ability to analyze collected data and tailor experiences to individuals, in tension with strict data minimization.

records.name: Certificate Management
records.definition: The activity of issuing, deploying, renewing, and revoking the digital certificates that transport encryption depends on.

records.name: Client Complexity
records.definition: The degree of additional effort a protective measure imposes on client implementations.

records.name: Developer Ergonomics
records.definition: The degree to which a system is convenient and pleasant for developers to work with.

records.name: Dynamic Query Flexibility
records.definition: The degree of freedom to vary a query's structure at runtime, constrained when inputs must be bound as parameters.

records.name: Ease of Initial Use
records.definition: The degree to which a system is easy to start using without upfront configuration.

records.name: Feature Exposure
records.definition: The degree to which functionality is made accessible, which broadens capability but enlarges the attack surface.

records.name: Formatting Flexibility
records.definition: The degree of latitude to present output in varied formats, constrained when encoding must be strict.

records.name: Input Flexibility
records.definition: The degree to which a system accepts varied or loosely-structured input, in tension with strict validation.

records.name: Key Operations
records.definition: The degree of operational burden imposed by generating, rotating, and safeguarding cryptographic keys.

records.name: Latency/Complexity
records.definition: The degree of added latency and complexity introduced by verifying every request rather than trusting a perimeter.

records.name: Operational Convenience
records.definition: The degree to which broad access makes day-to-day operations easier, in tension with least privilege.

records.name: Pipeline Complexity
records.definition: The degree of intricacy added to a delivery pipeline by embedding continuous checks within it.

records.name: Policy Maintenance
records.definition: The activity of keeping codified policies correct and current as requirements evolve.

records.name: Role Explosion
records.definition: The degree to which roles proliferate into many narrow definitions as access requirements grow.

records.name: Speed
records.definition: The degree to which delivery proceeds rapidly, in tension with the caution that managing risk requires.

records.name: Team Velocity
records.definition: The rate at which a team delivers completed work, which governance overhead can slow.

records.name: Usability
records.definition: The ease with which users can accomplish their goals with a system.

records.name: User Convenience
records.definition: The degree to which a system minimizes friction and effort for its users.

records.name: Remove Secret from Code
records.definition: A technique for deleting a credential from source and history and reading it from a secret store instead.

records.name: Secret Rotation
records.definition: A technique for replacing credentials on a schedule and after any exposure, so a leaked secret stops working.

records.name: Least-Privilege Credential
records.definition: A technique for issuing each caller a credential that grants only the operations it performs.

records.name: Centralize Policy
records.definition: A technique for evaluating every authorization decision through one policy model instead of scattered checks.

records.name: Server-Side Enforcement
records.definition: A technique for enforcing every security rule on the server, whatever the client checks.

records.name: Penetration Testing
records.definition: A technique for attacking a system under agreement to find the paths that bypass its controls.

records.name: Authorization Tests
records.definition: A technique for testing each protected operation with permitted and refused identities.

records.name: Field Redaction
records.definition: A technique for removing or masking sensitive fields before data is logged, exported or displayed.

records.name: Purpose Binding
records.definition: A technique for tagging personal data with the purpose it was collected for and refusing uses outside it.

records.name: Retention Policy
records.definition: A technique for declaring how long each class of data is kept and deleting it when the period ends.

records.name: Repository Secret Scan
records.definition: A technique for scanning source and history for credentials before a change is accepted.

records.name: Default Deny
records.definition: A technique for refusing every access that no rule explicitly allows.

records.name: Sandboxing
records.definition: A technique for running untrusted code with only the resources and permissions it is granted.

records.name: Network Segmentation
records.definition: A technique for dividing a network into zones whose traffic between them passes declared controls.
